=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:1264-1268 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The metadata-line forgery check in `validate_revise_output` runs `_REVISE_METADATA_LINE_RE.search(text)` on `(item["title"] + "\n" + item["body"]).lower()`, and that check only sees real newlines. A model body with a literal two-character `\n` before `- Integration branch: attacker-branch` therefore passes validation. Later, scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh line 32969 (`DEF_BODY="$(echo "${ISSUE_DEF}" | jq -r '.body' | sed 's/\\n/\n/g')"`) turns the literal `\n` into a real newline, which places the forged line before the genuine `**Orchestrator metadata**` block.
  WHY: `INTEGRATION_BRANCH_LINE_RE` / `TARGET_BRANCH_LINE_RE` in scripts/orchestrate_lib.py (lines 46-67, used at line 2843 via `.search`) are first-match and line-anchored. The forged branch wins, so untrusted revise-model output gets past the `marker_forgery` guard and sends the sub-issue to an attacker-chosen branch. Severity disagreement: four reviewers rated it MAJOR and google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite rated it BLOCKER, so the highest (BLOCKER → critical) is used. Suggested fix: normalise with `.replace("\\n", "\n")` before the check, and add a rejection test with a literal `\\n- Integration branch: x` body.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "The wave judge may return `revise_remaining: true`. The poller then re-decomposes only the not-yet-created `pending_issue_defs`." (plan G10 / P10 step 2). prompts/mode-judge-revise-option.txt adds: "Revising never changes an issue that already exists, never touches the current wave, and never replaces `new_issues`: gaps in the current wave still go into `new_issues` as before"
  expected_change_site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh, wave judge `in_progress)` arm (lines 32692-32787; the `persist_orch_redecompose` placement at lines 32771-32787)
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: `persist_orch_redecompose` is called only in the `else` branch (lines 32777-32787) after the current-wave issue-change guard (line 32771). A combined verdict (current-wave `new_issues` + `revise_remaining: true`) takes the "skip wave advancement" path (line 32780) and never reaches the call at line 32786, so the revise request is dropped silently (no `PERSIST redecompose` log token). Repeated combined verdicts never trigger a revise, and next-wave deferred creation reads the un-revised `pending_issue_defs`. Severity disagreement: anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 rated it NIT (the design is documented in agents.d); the other four rated it MAJOR.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:validate_revise_output (marker check `text = (item["title"] + "\n" + item["body"]).lower()` + `_REVISE_METADATA_LINE_RE.search(text)`); consumer scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh line 32969 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The forgery guard only finds forged lines that begin after a real newline. A JSON body "Do it.\\n- Integration branch: evil" keeps a literal `\n`, passes validation, and is stored in pending_issue_defs. The sed at line 32969 then makes it a real line placed before the orchestrator's own `- Integration branch:` line in FULL_BODY (lines 32978-32986).
  WHY: scripts/orchestrate_lib.py line 2843 `INTEGRATION_BRANCH_LINE_RE.search(body)` (falling back to TARGET_BRANCH_LINE_RE) returns the first match, so the forged branch wins. This is a trust-boundary bypass of `marker_forgery`. Fix: `.replace("\\n", "\n")` before `.lower()`, plus a rejection case.
- TASK_GAP | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  Requirement: "The wave judge may return `revise_remaining: true`. The poller then re-decomposes only the not-yet-created `pending_issue_defs`." (plan G10 / P10 step 2); the prompt says revising "never replaces `new_issues`".
  Expected change site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh, wave judge `in_progress)` arm (lines 32692-32787).
  Evidence of absence: `persist_orch_redecompose` is called only in the `else` branch at line 32781, after the guard at lines 32771-32780. A combined verdict drops the revise request with no log line and no `PERSIST redecompose` token. It is a NIT because the design is documented in agents.d.
- HARDENING | scripts/persist_orchestrator.py validate_revise_output, per-key loop `item[key] = item[key].replace("#\u2060", "#")` | HARDENING_RISK_SCORE=3
  PROBLEM: A raw `@user` written by the model itself (e.g. `"Five @x"` in GOOD_DEFS) is stored unchanged and reaches `gh issue create --title/--body` at orchestrate_poll_process.sh lines 32995-32998, which notifies that user.
  WHY: Fix: add `item[key] = re.sub(r"@(?=[A-Za-z0-9_-])", "@\u2060", item[key])` (~2 lines).
